message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Item | Description | |------|-------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you agree on). Points are earned by being the first to finish each round. | | **Players** | 2–10 (standard deck). | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Green, Blue, Yellow) × 25 cards each (one 0, two 1–9, two “Draw Two”, two “Skip”, two “Reverse”), plus 4 “Wild” and 4 “Wild Draw Four”. | | **Setup** | Shuffle the deck. Deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile; flip the top card to start the discard pile. | | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a Reverse card changes direction). | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn, you may play one card from your hand that matches either the color or the number/symbol of the top discard. If you have no playable card, you must draw one from the draw pile. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Special Cards** | • **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses play direction.
• **Wild** – You choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – You choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. (Can only be played if you have no matching color; otherwise, you can be challenged.) | | **Winning a Round** | When a player discards their last card, the round ends. All other players count the point value of the cards left in their hands: numbers = face value, Draw Two/Skip/Reverse = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. The winner adds those points to their score. | | **Game End** | First player to reach the agreed‑upon score (commonly 500) wins the game. | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep an eye on the discard pile** – you can often anticipate what the next player will need to play. 2. **Use Wilds strategically** – change the color when you’re low on cards or when you think the next player has none of that color. 3. **Challenge a Wild Draw Four** – if you suspect the player had a matching color, you can challenge them. If they were wrong, they must draw 4 cards; if they were right, you draw 6 cards instead. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
